title: How to Read a Lost THC COA and Lab Report Line by Line
excerpt: Learn how to read a Lost THC COA, from the batch code and ND results to the UI line, using real V4 and V2 lab reports. Read our step by step guide.
content:
To read a Lost THC COA, check four things in order: the header, the cannabinoid table, the contaminant panels and the reporting limits. Each one answers a different question about the sample the lab tested. This guide walks through one real report. It's the KCA Laboratories report for the Fruity Pebz OG strain of Lost THC V4 CB9A + THC-P Disposable 3G, batch LTLRV425-01.

We also cover the older reports for Lost THC V2 7.5g Live Resin Disposable Vape, which look different. For a general checklist that fits any hemp vape, see our guide to reading a hemp vape COA. This article sticks to the Lost THC reports and is for adults 21+ only.

Key Takeaways

  • The V4 Fruity Pebz OG report lists Delta-9 THCP at 47.1% and Delta-8 THC at 33.6%, with total Delta-9 THC not detected.
  • Delta-9 THCP and Delta-9 THC are different molecules, so read each row by its exact name.
  • The V4 reports (batch LTLRV425-01) cover heavy metals, pesticides, mycotoxins, residual solvents and microbials.
  • The older V2 reports are cannabinoid-only, and the KCA ones say "Batch: Not Specified".
  • A COA describes one tested sample. It doesn't describe effects, safety or legal status.

Two Lost THC lines, two reports

The two Lost THC products we carry have different paper trails. This table shows the headline figures exactly as the reports print them.

DetailLost THC V4 CB9A + THC-P Disposable 3GLost THC V2 7.5g Live Resin Disposable Vape
LabKCA LaboratoriesKCA Laboratories and PharmLabs San Diego
Report dateSeptember 2025July 2024 (KCA), November 2024 (PharmLabs)
Batch on reportLTLRV425-01Not Specified on the KCA reports
Delta-9 THCP45.8 to 47.1%1.81 to 2.22% (KCA), 5.18 to 5.59% (PharmLabs)
Delta-8 THC33.1 to 33.8%76.4 to 77.6% (KCA), 80.18 to 83.91% (PharmLabs)
Total Delta-9 THCND on all sixND on KCA; PharmLabs lists total THC at 0.06%
PanelsCannabinoids plus five contaminant panelsCannabinoids only

The report titles differ from our product names. The V2 reports are titled "LOST THC RAINBOW EDITION 7.5g Disposable" and the V4 reports "LOST THC Live Resin 3g Disposable". Match a report to a product by strain and date, not by title.

Start with the report header

The header sits at the top of page one. On the Fruity Pebz OG report it names the client as Lost Distribution, the lab as KCA Laboratories and the batch as LTLRV425-01. It also gives a sample ID and an expiration date of August 14, 2027. The sample arrived August 28, 2025, and the cannabinoids were tested September 12, 2025.

Check three things. The batch should match the code on your pack. The dates should fit the product's age. The lab should be one you can look up. Our guide to checking a Lost THC pack covers the pack side.

KCA's own site lists a PJLA ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation and the same KDA hemp license number the report prints, P_0058. ISO/IEC 17025 is an international standard for accrediting testing labs.

Reading the cannabinoid table

Page two holds the cannabinoid table. Each row is one compound, with a result and the lab's limits.

  • Percent: the compound's weight as a share of the sample. Fruity Pebz OG shows Delta-9 THCP at 47.1%.
  • mg/g: milligrams per gram. One percent equals 10 mg/g, so 47.1% is 471 mg/g.
  • LOD (limit of detection): the lowest amount the method can see.
  • LOQ (limit of quantitation): the lowest amount the method can measure with confidence.
  • ND (not detected): the method found nothing at or above its limit. It doesn't prove the compound is absent at every amount.

The report lists total cannabinoids at 83.4%. The remainder isn't itemized, so the rows won't add up to 100%.

What total Delta-9 THC means

KCA prints the formula on its reports: Total Delta-9 THC = Delta-9 THCA × 0.877 + Delta-9 THC. The 0.877 factor adjusts for the mass THCA loses when heat turns it into Delta-9 THC. On the Fruity Pebz OG report, that total is ND.

Delta-9 THCP is not Delta-9 THC

Delta-9 THCP, Delta-9 THC and Delta-8 THC are three separate compounds, and each gets its own row.

On the Fruity Pebz OG report, Delta-9 THCP reads 47.1% and Delta-8 THC reads 33.6%. Total Delta-9 THC reads ND. Across all six V4 reports, Delta-9 THCP runs 45.8 to 47.1% and total Delta-9 THC is ND on every one.

CB9A isn't a line item on any of the six V4 reports. A compound the lab doesn't list as an analyte is one the report can't speak to.

The contaminant panels

The pages after the cannabinoid table cover contaminants. The V4 reports run five panels, each with its own method.

  • Heavy metals (ICP-MS): arsenic, cadmium, lead and mercury, all not detected.
  • Pesticides (LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS): not detected for every analyte listed.
  • Mycotoxins: aflatoxins B1, B2, G1 and G2 plus ochratoxin A, not detected.
  • Residual solvents (HS-GC-MS): not detected for every analyte listed.
  • Microbials (PCR and plating): not detected, apart from two lines marked "<RL".

RL stands for reporting limit. A "<RL" line means the result fell below the lowest level the lab reports, so there's no number to read. On our worked example, the total aerobic count reads <RL. On the Bloo Dream report, yeast and mold does.

The appendix at the end lists the limit for every analyte. An ND or <RL tells you more once you know how low the test could see.

What a COA can't tell you

  • One sample, one batch. A report covers the sample tested. A pack with a different batch code isn't covered by LTLRV425-01.
  • Moisture content. The V4 reports mark it as not tested.
  • Older V2 reports. They are cannabinoid-only. The KCA ones, dated July 2024, say "Batch: Not Specified", so they can't be tied to a batch code on a pack.
  • Effects, safety and legality. A COA measures. It doesn't say how a product feels, whether it suits you or whether it's legal where you live.

Federal hemp rules also change on November 12 and December 11, 2026, and states set their own rules. A lab report can't answer that for you.

In the 90 days to October 28, 2026, roughly 3 in 4 Lost THC units ordered from Vape24 were the 7.5g line. That line has the cannabinoid-only reports.

A real example of an inconclusive result

The PharmLabs San Diego reports for Blue Zushi and GG#4, reported November 27, 2024, show how a lab handles a result it can't call. The Delta-9 THC row reads "UI", short for unidentified.

A lab note explains why. The Delta-9 result is inconclusive because other cannabinoids interfered in GC-MS/MS, and no interference showed up by HPLC. The same reports print THCA at 0.07% and total THC at 0.06%, which fits the formula, since 0.07 × 0.877 is about 0.06.

The lab didn't write ND or invent a number. Read UI as "not determined", never as "none".

Lost THC COA questions

What is a Lost THC COA?

A Lost THC COA is a third-party lab report on a sample of a Lost THC product. The reports we've read come from KCA Laboratories and PharmLabs San Diego, and they list cannabinoid results. The V4 reports add contaminant panels.

Does ND for total Delta-9 THC mean the vape has no THC?

No. ND means total Delta-9 THC wasn't detected on that report. Delta-9 THCP and Delta-8 THC are different compounds with their own rows, and the report lists them separately.

Why does a V2 report say Batch Not Specified?

The July 2024 KCA reports for the V2 line don't name a batch. They apply to the sample tested, but you can't match them to a batch code on a pack.

What does UI mean on a PharmLabs report?

UI means unidentified. On the Blue Zushi and GG#4 reports, the lab marked Delta-9 THC as inconclusive because of interference from other cannabinoids in GC-MS/MS. Read it as not determined.

Does the V4 report list CB9A?

No. CB9A isn't an analyte on any of the six V4 reports we read, so those reports can't confirm or rule out anything about it.

Lab reports describe what was measured in one sample. They aren't health advice, and this article makes no claim about effects or legal status. For adults 21+ only. Browse the Lost THC lineup, read our Lost THC vapes guide or the V2 vs V4 review.

title: HQD New Packaging and Logo Explained, Plus How to Verify
excerpt: HQD rebranded in November 2025 and changed its packaging in January 2026. See what changed and how to verify your HQD with the scratch-off code.
content:
The HQD new packaging and logo are part of a rebrand announced on November 20, 2025. HQD introduced the packaging on January 15, 2026, and upgraded its anti-counterfeiting label on April 21, 2026. As of November 6, 2026, we found no sign of another change on HQD's official news page.

This guide covers what changed, what we can and can't say about the old design, and how to confirm that any HQD device is genuine. We don't have photos of the old design, so the images here show the symbol, a recent pack and the label guide.

Key takeaways

  • HQD announced its rebrand on November 20, 2025, with a brighter orange, a Q symbol and a new slogan.
  • HQD new packaging followed on January 15, 2026. HQD says the product inside is unchanged.
  • HQD says old and new packs are both genuine and will coexist, but it hasn't given an end date.
  • Every HQD is checked the same way: scratch the code sticker, then scan the QR code.
  • We found no sign of a second rebrand as of November 6, 2026.
  • HQD SLYD 60K is one of the newest HQD releases we carry, sold as a kit with separate replacement pods.

HQD rebrand timeline

Every date below comes from HQD's own news posts, and together they show one rebrand rolled out in stages.

Date What HQD announced HQD source
Nov 20, 2025 Brand renewal with Brighter Orange and a new Q symbol Renewal launch
Nov 22, 2025 The thinking behind the new Q symbol Super Symbol story
Nov 24, 2025 Slogan "Let's Fresh the Moment" explained Brand philosophy
Jan 15, 2026 New packaging, with old and new packs coexisting New packaging post
Apr 21, 2026 Upgraded V2 anti-counterfeiting label Label V1 vs V2

What the new Q symbol means

The new mark is built from the Q in HQD, and HQD says the squared outer frame stands for intelligence while the circle inside it stands for openness. The dot is a stylized smoke particle, and the curved lines suggest airflow.

HQD pairs the symbol with a brighter orange that it says replaces an older, muted tone. The new slogan is "Let's Fresh the Moment," and HQD adds that its name stands for Humanity, Quest and Devotion.

HQD new packaging vs the old design

HQD's January 15, 2026 post says the new pack puts the brand symbol on the front, with bolder branding and a cleaner look. It also uses the new orange.

HQD hasn't published a description of the old design, so we won't guess at details. It does say the product inside is unchanged and both designs are genuine. HQD says the two will coexist during the rollout, with no end date given.

How to verify your HQD

HQD says the same check works on every package, old or new.

  1. Find the code sticker on the package.
  2. Scratch off the coating to reveal the security code.
  3. Scan the QR code, or enter the code at hqdtech.com/verification.

HQD also lists yz.hqdtech.com as a second verification page.

A guide to finding the label and telling the two versions apart.

Label V1 and V2

HQD says you may now see two label versions, and V1 has a round pattern with staggered letters and a multicolor metallic refraction. V2 mixes square and round elements and adds a nuclear track membrane.

HQD's own V2 test is simple: dab a colored marker on the label, let it dry, then wipe it clean. A sharp "HQD" mark in the same color should appear. That test is HQD's method, and we haven't run it ourselves.

Type the web address yourself

HQD's label post lists one verification site as hgdtech.com, with a g instead of a q. When we checked on November 6, 2026, that spelling didn't return a working page. Use hqdtech.com, and type it in rather than following a link.

Will HQD rebrand again?

We found no sign of it. We read both pages of HQD's news section, 11 posts from October 2025 to July 2026, plus its brand and media kit pages.

The only forward-looking line is general, as HQD says it will keep introducing new flavors and designs. It gives no dates and names no new logo or packaging. We'll update this page if that changes.

New HQD products since the rebrand

Per HQD, nothing about the device inside a new pack changes, so the specs on each product page still apply.

The newest HQD release we carry is SLYD 60K, which HQD lists under New Arrival on its site. The HQD SLYD 60K kit is modular, with a 900 mAh magnetic power bank that holds a 500 mAh disposable pod with a 20 mL tank. HQD rates it for up to 60,000 puffs.

HQD SLYD multipack in Pineapple Mtn Dew, a recent HQD release.

When a pod runs out, you swap it and keep the power bank, and replacement SLYD 60K pods are sold separately. Our SLYD 60K review covers the specs in detail.

For the full lineup, read our HQD vape guide and the best HQD vapes comparison. You can also browse the HQD collection or all disposable vapes.

HQD rebrand FAQ

Did HQD change its logo?

Yes. In November 2025, HQD introduced a redrawn Q symbol with a squared frame, an inner circle and a smoke-particle dot, plus a brighter orange.

Is the new HQD packaging genuine?

Yes, according to HQD. It says new and old packaging are both 100% genuine and that only the exterior differs. You can confirm any pack with the scratch-off code at hqdtech.com/verification.

How long will old and new packs coexist?

HQD hasn't said. Its January 15, 2026 post describes a transition period but gives no end date.

What does HQD stand for?

HQD says the name stands for Humanity, Quest and Devotion.

Which new HQD products do you carry?

HQD SLYD 60K, a modular kit with a replaceable pod. HQD lists it under New Arrival. The kit and the pods have separate product pages.

What is HQD's new slogan?

The new slogan is "Let's Fresh the Moment," announced with the brand renewal in November 2025.

Information on this page comes from HQD's published posts and our own checks as of November 6, 2026. WARNING: Vape products may contain nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical. For adults 21+ only.

title: HQD SLYD 60K Review, Specs and Replacement Pod Guide
excerpt: Read our HQD SLYD 60K review with real specs, ECO and BOOST puff ratings, charging times, 10 flavors and what to know before buying a kit or spare pod.
content:
The HQD SLYD 60K review starts with one fact: it's a rechargeable vape kit that pairs a 900mAh power bank with a swappable 20mL pod. HQD rates it for up to 60K puffs in ECO mode and 45K in BOOST mode, at 5% nicotine, in 10 flavors.

This HQD SLYD 60K review is built from HQD's specifications, both user manuals, the retail box and HQD's product page. It isn't based on weeks of daily use, and HQD hasn't published tasting notes, so we stick to what the documents support and say where they stop.

HQD SLYD 60K Vape Kit

900mAh power bank and 20mL pod, rated up to 60K puffs

View the kit

HQD SLYD 60K Replacement Pod

20mL, 5% nicotine, 10 flavors, fits the SLYD power bank

View the pod

Key takeaways

  • HQD rates the SLYD for up to 60000 puffs in ECO mode and 45000 puffs in BOOST mode.
  • It's a two-part system: a 900mAh Type-C power bank and a 500mAh, 20mL pod.
  • HQD offers 10 flavors in 6 device colors, at a single 5% nicotine strength.
  • No charging cable is listed in the box, and a pod only recharges through the SLYD power bank.
  • Replacement pods are sold separately, so you keep the power bank when a pod runs out.

HQD SLYD 60K specs at a glance

The SLYD sells as a kit or as a spare pod, and both use the same pod. The table covers each.

FeatureHQD SLYD 60K kitSLYD 60K replacement pod
In the boxPower bank, one pod and a manualOne pod and a manual
Size101.6 x 54.6 x 30 mm96 x 34.7 x 25.5 mm
E-liquid20 mL20 mL
Nicotine5% (50 mg/mL)5% (50 mg/mL)
Battery900 mAh power bank, 500 mAh pod500 mAh pod
Puff rating60000 ECO, 45000 BOOST60K ECO, 45K BOOST
Coil1.0 Ω dual mesh1.0 Ω dual mesh
ChargingType-C power bank, magnetic podMagnetic, through the SLYD power bank only

Those figures come from HQD's manuals, box artwork and product page. HQD's 1400mAh headline is the 900mAh power bank and the 500mAh pod added together, not a single battery.

How many puffs does it last?

HQD rates the SLYD at up to 60K puffs in ECO mode and up to 45K puffs in BOOST mode. ECO gives balanced vapor and consistent flavor. BOOST raises power output for maximum vapor volume, and its rating is 15K puffs lower.

Treat both numbers as manufacturer ceilings. Your draw length and mode change the real result. As simple division, 200 puffs a day lasts 300 days in ECO and 225 days in BOOST. That's math, not a guarantee.

Each pod holds 20mL behind a visible window, so you can check the liquid level at a glance. A 1.0 Ω dual mesh coil heats the e-liquid, and HQD describes the taste as rich and smooth. We can't confirm that without long-term use.

The pod carries 5% nicotine, or 50 mg/mL, and HQD lists no other strength for the SLYD. Nicotine is addictive. For more on how ratings work across the range, read our guide to how many puffs an HQD vape lasts.

Power bank and pod, explained

The SLYD splits into two parts. The 900mAh power bank holds the pod in a slide-in magnetic seat and charges it through contacts. The pod has its own 500mAh battery and the coil.

A full pod charge takes about 40 minutes through the power bank. The power bank takes about 65 minutes over Type-C. One button switches between ECO and BOOST, and the screen shows the active mode and the charge status. HQD says a new pod starts in BOOST.

The box holds only the kit and a user manual. No charging cable is listed, and Vape24 has confirmed none ships with it, so plan on a USB-C cable you already own.

HQD's manual adds a few care rules. Don't charge it unattended or overnight, and keep it away from flammable materials. Charge it only between 32°F and 113°F (0°C to 45°C), so not in freezing cold or in the heat. It also says to clean the magnetic contacts weekly, and its fix for a pod that won't charge is to align and clean them. Our HQD charging guide covers the rest of the range.

Flavors and colors

HQD offers 10 flavors and pairs each with a device color. The pods are black in every flavor, so the flavor name is printed on the box.

  • Black Ice in black
  • Grape Slush in purple
  • Blue Slush in blue
  • Watermelon Ice and Hawaiian Punch in red
  • Polar Ice and Miami Mint in green
  • Mexico Mango, Pineapple Mtn Dew and Strawberry Banana in yellow

HQD hasn't published tasting notes, so we won't describe flavors we can't source. The names point to icy and menthol profiles (Black Ice, Watermelon Ice, Polar Ice, Miami Mint). They also point to slush flavors (Grape Slush, Blue Slush) and fruit flavors (Hawaiian Punch, Mexico Mango, Pineapple Mtn Dew, Strawberry Banana). Stock changes by flavor, so check each product page.

Six device colors cover all 10 flavors.

Kit or replacement pod?

Buy the HQD SLYD 60K kit if you don't own a SLYD power bank. It's the only version with the power bank, and it includes your first pod.

Buy a SLYD 60K replacement pod when you already have the power bank. A pod has no charging port of its own, so on its own it's a refill, not a device.

HQD's manual says a pod keeps its last power setting when it's used on its own, but it can only recharge through the power bank.

The pod isn't locked to the SLYD power bank. It's compatible with multiple devices from other brands, including the RAZ VUE 50K and the RAZ VUE 70K Halloween Edition, which makes it a flexible refill. HQD calls the system cross and multi compatible but hasn't published a full list of devices, so check that yours is a match before you buy.

Where the SLYD fits in HQD's lineup

Our own sales show where HQD buyers land. In the 90 days to November 2, 2026, the HQD Everest 25K made up about 48% of the HQD units Vape24 sold. The HQD Mars 8000 came second at about 20%.

The SLYD is a different kind of device. The Everest is a disposable. The SLYD splits the power bank from the pod, so you can change flavors without buying a new battery.

The HQD Snap 50K kit is the other modular HQD device we carry. It uses a nicotine alternative called Nixodine instead of nicotine, so it isn't a like-for-like swap. Our HQD vape guide and best HQD vapes roundup compare the full range, and the HQD brand page lists everything in stock.

Pros and cons, plus our verdict

What works

  • Up to 60000 puffs in ECO mode from one 20mL pod, per HQD
  • Swappable pods, so a new flavor doesn't mean a new battery
  • A visible pod window, two power modes and a screen that shows mode and charge
  • A Type-C power bank and a pod that charges in about 40 minutes
  • 10 flavors in 6 colors, with pods sold separately
  • The pod is compatible with multiple devices from other brands, including the RAZ VUE 50K and the RAZ VUE 70K Halloween Edition

What to watch

  • No charging cable in the box
  • A pod has no charging port of its own
  • One strength only, at 5% nicotine
  • No published tasting notes and little long-term owner feedback so far
  • HQD hasn't published a full list of compatible devices

Our HQD SLYD 60K review verdict is simple. On paper, it suits adults who want the 60K-puff ECO rating and the option to swap pods without replacing the battery.

The trade-offs are practical. Bring your own cable, and confirm a non-HQD device is a match before you pair it with a SLYD pod. We'll update this HQD SLYD 60K review as real-world feedback comes in.

SLYD 60K questions answered

How many puffs does the HQD SLYD 60K last?

HQD rates the SLYD for up to 60000 puffs in ECO mode and up to 45000 puffs in BOOST mode from one 20mL pod. Those are manufacturer ratings, and your draw style changes the real number. At 200 puffs a day, ECO works out to 300 days.

How much nicotine does the HQD SLYD 60K have?

The SLYD pod contains 5% nicotine, or 50 mg/mL, as printed on the box and in HQD's pod manual. HQD lists one strength for the line, so every flavor is the same. Nicotine is addictive, and the product is for adults 21 and over.

Does the HQD SLYD 60K come with a charger?

No charging cable is listed in the box, which holds the kit and a user manual, and Vape24 has confirmed none ships with it. Use your own USB-C cable. The pod charges through the power bank, and the power bank charges over Type-C.

How long does the SLYD 60K take to charge?

A full pod charge takes about 40 minutes through the power bank's magnetic contacts. The power bank takes about 65 minutes over Type-C. HQD's manual says not to charge it unattended or overnight.

Can you buy replacement pods for the SLYD 60K?

Yes. Each SLYD 60K replacement pod is sold separately in the same 10 flavors, with 20mL of e-liquid, its own 500mAh battery and a 1.0 Ω dual mesh coil. It's also compatible with multiple devices from other brands, including the RAZ VUE 50K and the RAZ VUE 70K Halloween Edition.

What's the difference between ECO and BOOST mode?

ECO mode delivers balanced vapor and consistent flavor, and it's rated for up to 60K puffs. BOOST mode raises power output for maximum vapor volume and is rated for up to 45K puffs. A new pod starts in BOOST, and a short press of the button switches modes.

title: HQD vs Fume Zero Nicotine Vapes, Which Should You Buy
excerpt: HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 or Fume Pro 30K in 0% nicotine? Compare puffs, 18mL vs 22mL tanks, batteries and flavors, then shop the one that suits you.
content:
The HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero Nicotine and the Fume Pro 30K Zero Nicotine are the two 0% nicotine disposable vapes we stock. The HQD is rated for 9000+ puffs from an 18mL tank and comes in five flavors. The Fume is rated for up to 30000 puffs from 22mL and comes in two.

If you want a zero nicotine vape, it comes down to puff rating, tank size and flavor. The Fume lasts longer on paper. The HQD has more flavors.

Key takeaways

  • The Fume Pro 30K Zero is rated for up to 30000 puffs, over three times the HQD's 9000+.
  • The Fume holds 22mL of e-liquid and the HQD holds 18mL.
  • The HQD comes in five flavors and the Fume in two.
  • With 0% nicotine the throat hit is softer and the flavor leads.
  • Both are 0% nicotine, dual mesh, USB-C rechargeable and sold to adults 21 and over only.

Why choose a 0% nicotine vape?

Taking nicotine out changes the experience in a few practical ways.

  • Softer throat hit. With no nicotine, the draw is smoother, so the flavor leads.
  • No strength to pick. There's no 3% or 5% decision, just a flavor.
  • A nicotine-free choice for adults who prefer none in their device.
  • An easy swap between sessions on a nicotine device.

The liquid still contains propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin and flavoring. Neither device is sold as a quit aid, and we make no health claims. Both are for adults 21 and over only.

The two devices

HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero

The HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero Nicotine is the 0% edition of the 5% Cuvie Plus 2.0. It has an 18mL prefilled tank, a dual mesh coil rated at 1.4 ohm and an LCD screen. A 600mAh battery charges over USB-C.

Five flavors are available: Black Ice, Blueberry Lemonade, Mint, Grape and Strawberry Banana. Black Ice is blackberry with menthol, and Strawberry Banana is the creamy fruit blend.

Fume Pro 30K Zero

The Fume Pro 30K Zero Nicotine is the 0% edition of the 5% Fume Pro 30K. It holds 22mL behind dual mesh coils, with a 750mAh USB-C battery and a full-screen display for battery and e-liquid levels. It's draw-activated, so there are no buttons.

It comes in Banana Candy and Lush Ice. Banana Candy is sweet with no cooling, and Lush Ice is watermelon with a menthol chill.

Which one lasts longer?

On paper, the Fume. Its rating of up to 30K puffs is more than three times the 9000 on the HQD, and its tank holds 4mL more. Both numbers are ceilings, since draw length changes the real count.

A bigger tank means fewer swaps, which suits daily use. The HQD's smaller tank suits shorter use. Our guide on how long disposable vapes last explains why puff ratings vary.

Charging both

Both charge over USB-C. The HQD cable isn't included, so use any USB-C cable you own. Both screens show battery level, so top up before either goes flat.

Winners by category

  • Longest rated run: Fume Pro 30K Zero, up to 30000 puffs.
  • Biggest tank: Fume Pro 30K Zero, 22mL.
  • Most flavors: HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero, five against two.
  • Smaller commitment: HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero, 9000+ puffs.

Zero or 5% versions?

The 5% versions have far longer flavor lists, and they contain nicotine. Browse every zero nicotine vape we carry, or see our 30K puff vapes guide for higher-strength options.

Brand pages: HQD and Fume. The HQD vape guide covers the rest of that brand.

Frequently asked questions

Do these vapes contain any nicotine?

No. Both e-liquids are 0% nicotine. They still contain propylene glycol, vegetable glycerin and flavoring, and both are sold to adults 21 and over only.

Which zero nicotine vape lasts longer?

On paper, the Fume Pro 30K Zero Nicotine, rated for up to 30000 puffs from 22mL. The HQD Cuvie Plus 2.0 Zero Nicotine is rated for 9000+ puffs from 18mL. Draw length changes the real count, so treat both as ceilings.

What flavors does each one come in?

The HQD comes in Black Ice, Blueberry Lemonade, Mint, Grape and Strawberry Banana. The Fume comes in Banana Candy and Lush Ice. Every flavor on both is 0%.

Do they need a charger?

Both recharge over USB-C. The HQD cable isn't included, so use any USB-C cable you already own.

Is a nicotine-free vape a way to quit?

We don't sell it as one and make no health claims. It's a flavor option without nicotine for adults 21 and over. Anyone who wants help quitting should talk to a doctor.

title: Is Lost THC Real? How to Check the Hologram and Batch
excerpt: Is Lost THC real? Check the hologram, QR code and batch code, then match the batch to a lab report. Read our step-by-step guide before you buy.
content:
Is Lost THC real? You can check a Lost THC vape in three steps. Confirm where you bought it, look for the three markers the brand names on its packaging, and match the batch code to a lab report. Each check has limits, and this guide spells them out.

The brand says genuine packaging carries a hologram, a QR code and a printed batch code. No single mark settles it, so use all three with the lab report. This guide is for adults 21+ and covers authenticity only.

It doesn't say whether a hemp product is legal where you live. Federal hemp rules change on December 11, 2026, and states set their own, so check yours before you buy. Our Hemp & CBD guides cover that side. For the full lineup, lab reports and shipping states, see our Lost THC vapes guide.

Key Takeaways

  • The brand says it publishes no list of authorized retailers and calls LostTHC.com its only official store (read October 28, 2026).
  • The brand names three markers on genuine packaging: a hologram, a QR code and a printed batch code.
  • The V4 3G lab reports list batch LTLRV425-01 with an expiry of August 14, 2027. The July 2024 V2 reports say "Batch: Not Specified".
  • Both labs print ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation on their reports, and you can check the lab itself.
  • A hologram or a lab report alone isn't proof. Match the pack, the batch code and the report together.

Check the seller and the pack

Start with where you bought it

The brand's own brand-protection page says LostTHC.com is "the ONLY official website" operated and authorized by Lost THC (read October 28, 2026). It names lost-thc.com, with a hyphen, as a domain that "is not owned, operated, or authorized by Lost THC."

The same page says the brand doesn't currently publish a list of authorized retailers. So no official list exists to check any shop against, including ours. Vape24 is a retailer, not the brand.

We state that the Lost THC units we ship carry the brand hologram. You can see what we carry on our Lost THC brand page.

Look for three markers on the pack

The brand names three things on genuine packaging. Each one asks the same question: does this unit trace to a tested batch?

  • Hologram: the brand says it is applied to genuine packaging. We have no sourced description of its look or position, so we give none.
  • QR code: the brand says a genuine code resolves to the lab report for that batch on its site. A code that leads elsewhere is a problem.
  • Batch code: printed on the unit. The brand says to look it up against its certificates of analysis.

The brand says a unit with none of the three lacks the markers of a genuine product. Write down the batch code before anything else. Every step below uses it.

What the lab reports list

We carry two Lost THC lines, Lost THC V2 7.5g Live Resin Disposable Vape and Lost THC V4 CB9A + THC-P Disposable 3G, and hold lab reports for both. The client named on every report is Lost Distribution. We read them on October 28, 2026, and this table lists only what the reports measure.

ItemV2 7.5g Live ResinV4 3G
Strains with a report7 of 86 of 6
Batch printed on reportsKCA: "Not Specified"LTLRV425-01, exp August 14, 2027

Delta-9 THCP1.81% to 5.59%45.8% to 47.1%
Total Delta-9 THCNot detected (KCA); 0.06% total THC (PharmLabs)Not detected

Delta-9 THCP is a separate cannabinoid from Delta-9 THC. These are the labs' figures, not product claims. The V2 reports date from 2024 and the V4 reports from September 2025. Our V2 vs V4 review sets the two lines side by side.

Match your batch to a report

Compare the batch code on your pack with the batch on the report. The six V4 3G reports from KCA Laboratories all print batch LTLRV425-01. If your V4 pack reads that code, it matches those reports.

A different code isn't automatically a problem, since a product can be made in more than one batch. Ask the seller which report covers your pack.

The V2 reports have no batch to match

The July 2024 KCA reports for the V2 7.5g line print "Batch: Not Specified". With no batch on the report, a pack's batch code can't be tied to those five reports. That is a real limit.

You can still compare the client name, the lab, the strain, the sample ID and the dates. KCA received its samples on July 22, 2024 and tested them on July 25, 2024. PharmLabs San Diego reported on November 27, 2024. A match on those details is consistent with your pack. It doesn't prove your unit was tested.

The brand's own COA page lists its current products. When we looked on October 28, 2026, it didn't show batch LTLRV425-01 or a V4 3G product. The brand page doesn't say how earlier generations are handled. That isn't evidence about your unit either way, so the reports above are what we can match.

Check the lab report is real

A logo on a PDF proves little. Check the lab. Both labs on these reports state ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation. For the rest of the report, see our Lost THC COA walkthrough and the general guide to reading a hemp vape COA.

  • Read the lab name and accreditation number. KCA Laboratories lists PJLA accreditation number 108651 on its site (read October 28, 2026).
  • Look the lab up with its accrediting body. PJLA runs a public "Search Accredited Organizations" directory at pjlabs.com.
  • PharmLabs San Diego prints accreditation number L17-427-1. We couldn't confirm that listing, so ask the lab.
  • PharmLabs reports say "Scan the QR code to verify authenticity". Scan it and check where it lands.
  • KCA's site describes no self-serve check. Email [email protected] with the sample ID and ask.

When a check doesn't match

So, is Lost THC real? For one unit, only the pack, batch code and report together can answer that. A hologram or a lab report alone isn't proof. Anything printed can be copied, and a report can describe a different batch than your unit. Even a full match only shows your unit traces to a tested batch.

If something doesn't match, take these steps:

  • Keep the unit and the packaging, and photograph the batch code, the hologram and the QR code.
  • Contact the seller with your order number and the photos. Our support team can look at orders from Vape24.
  • Ask the brand. Its page says, "When in doubt, contact Lost THC directly before purchasing."
  • Hold off on using the unit until you have an answer.

Lost THC is a real brand with an official store at LostTHC.com. Whether one unit is genuine depends on that unit. Check the hologram, the QR code and the batch code the brand names, then match the batch to a lab report.

We have no report for OG Kush, even though the store lists it in this line. We won't stretch the other strains' numbers to cover it. The KCA reports also say Batch: Not Specified, so they can't be tied to a batch.

The reports run eight pages. They cover heavy metals, pesticides, mycotoxins, residual solvents and microbials, and nothing was detected. Two microbial lines read below the reporting limit, total aerobic count on Fruity Pebz OG and yeast and mold on Bloo Dream.

Moisture content wasn't tested. CB9A is in the product name but isn't an analyte on any of the six reports, so the reports can't speak to it. If CB9A matters to your choice, ask our team for a report that tests it.

title: RAZ VUE 70K Christmas Edition Review, Flavors and Pods
excerpt: Our RAZ VUE 70K Christmas Edition review covers the 16mL pod, the Peppermint Candy Cane and Watermelon Ice flavors, and how to reuse the bank. Read it.
content:
The RAZ VUE 70K Christmas Edition kit pairs a 16mL pod with a rechargeable power bank. It comes in two seasonal flavors, Peppermint Candy Cane and Watermelon Ice. RAZ rates the pod at up to 70000 puffs in Normal Mode.

This review covers the device, both flavors and the part many buyers miss. The power bank is yours to keep, so the matching Christmas Edition pod is all you need to refill.

Key takeaways

  • RAZ rates the pod at up to 70000 puffs in Normal Mode and about 35K in Boost Mode.
  • Each pod holds 16mL of 5% nicotine salt (50mg/mL) behind a dual mesh coil.
  • The power bank is reusable. Dock a fresh Christmas Edition pod and keep going.
  • Peppermint Candy Cane leans cool and sweet. Watermelon Ice pairs the fruit with a menthol chill.
  • It's a seasonal run, so a flavor that sells out may not return.

First look and specs

SpecChristmas Edition 70KVUE 50K kit
Puff ratingUp to 70000 (Normal Mode)50000
Pod fill16mL13mL
CoilDual meshDual mesh
Flavors2 seasonalWider menu

The VUE 50K kit uses the same pod-and-bank idea. Pick the Christmas Edition for the bigger pod and the holiday flavors.

Each kit ships with one prefilled pod and one rechargeable power bank, and it arrives pre-charged. The pod holds the e-liquid, the dual mesh coil and a small battery of its own. The bank docks on and tops it up as you go.

An LED readout shows battery and mode. The power bank carries a 1000mAh battery and the pod has its own 200mAh cell. When the bank runs low, recharge it over USB-C.

Peppermint Candy Cane and Watermelon Ice

Two flavors, two moods. One is a candy cane pulled off the tree. The other is a cold slice of watermelon.

Peppermint Candy Cane

The first draw opens with a refreshing peppermint burst. It's cool and clean, with a subtle sweetness that softens the edges.

On the exhale, the sweetness settles into a candy cane finish. Think sugar and mint together, not a bare menthol blast.

The dual mesh coil gives smooth, consistent hits from one puff to the next. It suits cold nights, hot drinks and the last hour of a long holiday evening.

Watermelon Ice

Juicy, ripe watermelon forms the base. It reads like a chilled slice on a summer afternoon, a bright change from the heavy flavors of the season.

The ice shows up late. It kicks in on the back end of the draw and cools the finish without drowning the fruit, so the sweetness stays in front.

Menthol fans who also want sweetness tend to love this profile. It's one of the most in-demand flavors across the VUE line.

Which flavor should you pick?

  • Pick Peppermint Candy Cane for a cool, sweet, candy cane mint.
  • Pick Watermelon Ice for juicy fruit with a menthol chill.
  • Can't decide? Both are 5%, so strength won't settle it.

Performance, modes and nicotine

RAZ rates the Christmas Edition at up to 70000 puffs in Normal Mode. Boost Mode trades range for a hotter hit and drops the rating to about 35K.

Those are manufacturer ratings taken on short draws, so heavy use lands lower. Our guide on how long disposable vapes last explains why.

Each pod holds 16mL of 5% nicotine salt, which is 50mg/mL, behind a dual mesh coil. That's a high-nicotine pod with no lower strength in the Christmas run. This product contains nicotine, and sales are restricted to adults 21 and over.

Keep the bank, swap the pod

This is where the kit beats a sealed disposable. The power bank outlasts the pod.

When a pod runs dry, keep the bank and dock a fresh one. The Christmas Edition replacement pod comes in both flavors, so you can repeat a favorite or switch.

That pod also fits other VUE 70K kits and the bank from the RAZ RYL Vue 70K kit.

The kit is a RAZ VUE 70K, but its matching pod is listed under the RAZ RYL Vue line. Don't let the name on the pod page throw you.

Pros, cons and verdict

What we like

  • A 16mL pod rated for up to 70000 puffs in Normal Mode.
  • A reusable power bank, so later pods are refills.
  • Two clear, seasonal flavors.
  • Ships pre-charged and ready to use.

Room to improve

  • Only two flavors, and the run is seasonal.
  • 5% only, with no lower-strength option.

Who should buy it?

  • New to pod-and-bank devices: take the kit, which includes the bank.
  • Already own a VUE 70K bank: skip the kit and buy the pod.
  • Want a seasonal flavor to match the month: either flavor delivers it.

Verdict

The Christmas Edition is an easy pick if you want a big pod, a reusable bank and a seasonal flavor. Start with the kit, then add a Christmas Edition pod when the first one runs out.

Peppermint on a cold night, watermelon chill after the feast. Either way, it's a holiday device for adults 21 and over.

title: Snoozy Gummies Lineup, Sleep, Focus and Energy Picks

content:
Snoozy gummies come in three formulas, and Vape24 carries all of them. Good Night's Sleep is a THC-free CBD and CBN gummy. Highly In Focus and Feel Good Energy each hold 5mg of Delta 9 THC per gummy.

Every pack has 20 gummies. That's 100mg of Delta 9 per daytime pack and 200mg each of CBD and CBN per sleep pack.

Key takeaways

  • Good Night's Sleep has 10mg of CBD and 10mg of CBN per gummy, with no THC.
  • Highly In Focus has 5mg of Delta 9, 20mg of CBD and 5mg of CBG per gummy.
  • Feel Good Energy has 5mg of Delta 9, 5mg of CBD and 5mg of CBG per gummy.

Snoozy pairs cannabinoids with plant extracts and lists them as ingredients, not proven effects. We do the same. Delta 9 is intoxicating, so only Good Night's Sleep is THC-free.

Good Night's Sleep gummies

Good Night's Sleep has 10mg of CBD and 10mg of CBN in every raspberry gummy. It also holds 25mg of L-theanine and 10mg of chamomile. The label calls it vegan, fast acting and melatonin-free.

The lab report for batch GNS-1489, from SC Labs, lists total THC as not detected. That makes it the one Snoozy gummy for shoppers who want no THC at all.

CBN is a non-intoxicating hemp cannabinoid many people associate with nighttime. That's an association, not a promised result, and everyone responds differently. It may cause drowsiness, so skip driving afterward.

Want a THC bedtime option instead? Our Jelly Signature Snooze gummies carry 5mg of Delta 9 and 20mg of CBN per gummy, with 40 in a pack.

The two Delta 9 gummies

Highly In Focus

Highly In Focus is a pineapple gummy with 5mg of Delta 9, 20mg of CBD and 5mg of CBG each. L-theanine joins four plant extracts: Lion's Mane, ginger root, sage and gotu kola. Each gummy has 2g of sugar.

The label says to eat one gummy. Effects can begin in as little as 15 minutes, but full effect can take 2 hours or more, so wait before taking another. Don't drive or operate machinery afterward.

Reviewers on the maker's page mention taste and a calm head feel. One felt tired instead of focused, and another found the head effect strong. Results vary with tolerance, body weight and what you've eaten.

Feel Good Energy

Feel Good Energy is a sour watermelon gummy with 5mg of Delta 9, 5mg of CBD and 5mg of CBG each. The blend adds L-theanine, Cordyceps, Rhodiola, Panax ginseng and vitamin B12. Each gummy has 2g of sugar.

Taste gets the most praise from reviewers on the maker's page. A couple call one gummy mild, and one found the effect short. That fits a 5mg dose, so how it lands depends on your tolerance.

The directions match Highly In Focus. Take one gummy and wait before you eat another.

What the lab reports show

Each Snoozy product page links its certificate of analysis. The Highly In Focus COA from Bluebonnet Labs, batch HIF-1339, measured about 4.8mg of Delta 9, 19.5mg of CBD and 5.0mg of CBG per gummy. The label says 5mg, 20mg and 5mg.

The Good Night's Sleep COA (batch GNS-1489, SC Labs) and the Feel Good Energy COA (batch FGE-1360, Bluebonnet Labs) are linked too. Product pages list label values. Measured numbers differ a little by batch, so read the report for exact figures.

Which Snoozy gummy fits you?

  • Pick Good Night's Sleep if you want an evening gummy with no THC.
  • Pick Highly In Focus if you want 5mg of Delta 9 with 20mg of CBD alongside.
  • Pick Feel Good Energy if you want an even 5mg split of Delta 9, CBD and CBG.

Start with one gummy and keep every hemp product away from children and pets. Delta 9 is intoxicating, and none of these replaces advice from a doctor.
